newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds close lower, but outlook firm.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds close lower, but outlook firm.

text.p: Argentine bonds closed a shade lower on profit-taking Friday, but were seen switching back to gains early next week, dealers said.

"The market looks good to us. Even though prices eased today, there was an undercurrent of buying and the drop in U.S. long bond yields bodes very well for local fixed-income investments," one dealer said.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 shed 1/4 to 94-5/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.70 to 121.0.

"Local bond prices are now strictly conditioned by U.S. Treasuries, which were boosted today by a low producer price index and a rise in the dollar against the mark," another dealer at a foreign-based bank said.
"That's why as soon as bond prices here consolidate, they should head quickly back up again," he said.
The U.S. long bond yield dropped to 6.53 percent Friday after setting a seven-month low of 6.56 percent Wednesday.
